database_summary: This is a movie metadata database (SQLite) containing a central Movie table plus many lookup/dimension tables for genre, language, country, location and person entities. Relationship (bridge) tables starting with M_ (M_Genre, M_Language, M_Country, M_Location, M_Cast, M_Director, M_Producer) implement many-to-many links between Movie and those dimensions. Data appears static/current (catalog of movies and associations) rather than time-series or event logs.

accepted.name: movie_basic
accepted.description: Normalized projection of the Movie table that preserves canonical identifiers and key measures. Use this as the clean movie base for joins, aggregations, or ranking. It ensures types are preserved and exposes year, rating, num_votes for downstream calculations. | Use for: List movies with ratings or votes; join movies to genres/people/countries; filter movies by year/rating/votes; compute aggregates per movie.

accepted.name: movie_with_genres
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  m."MID",
  m."title",
  m."year",
  mg."GID",
  g."Name" AS "Name",
  mg."ID"
FROM "Movie" m
JOIN "M_Genre" mg ON m."MID" = mg."MID"
LEFT JOIN "Genre" g ON mg."GID" = g."GID"
accepted.description: Denormalized movie-to-genre relation: one row per movie-genre assignment including human-readable genre Name. Useful for questions about counts or lists of genres per movie, top genres, or filtering movies by genre. | Use for: Which genres a movie belongs to; count movies per genre; filter movies by genre name; list movies for a genre.

accepted.name: movie_with_languages
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  m."MID",
  m."title",
  m."year",
  ml."LAID",
  l."Name" AS "Name",
  ml."ID"
FROM "Movie" m
JOIN "M_Language" ml ON m."MID" = ml."MID"
LEFT JOIN "Language" l ON ml."LAID" = l."LAID"
accepted.description: Denormalized movie-to-language relation: one row per movie-language assignment with language Name. Useful for filtering or aggregating movies by language. | Use for: Count movies by language; list movies in a specific language; join languages with ratings/votes.

accepted.name: movie_with_countries
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  m."MID",
  m."title",
  m."year",
  mc."CID",
  c."Name" AS "Name",
  mc."ID"
FROM "Movie" m
JOIN "M_Country" mc ON m."MID" = mc."MID"
LEFT JOIN "Country" c ON mc."CID" = c."CID"
accepted.description: Denormalized movie-to-country relation: one row per movie-country assignment with country Name. Use to analyze production countries or filter movies by country. | Use for: Which countries produced a movie; count movies by country; filter movies by country name.

accepted.name: movie_cast_members
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  m."MID",
  m."title",
  mc."PID",
  p."Name" AS "Name",
  p."Gender" AS "Gender",
  mc."ID"
FROM "Movie" m
JOIN "M_Cast" mc ON m."MID" = mc."MID"
LEFT JOIN "Person" p ON mc."PID" = p."PID"
accepted.description: Denormalized movie-to-cast relation: one row per movie-cast assignment with person Name and Gender. Useful for actor-centric queries, actor counts per movie, or filtering movies by cast member. | Use for: List actors in a movie; count movies per actor; filter movies by actor gender; join actor info with movie ratings.

accepted.name: people_film_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p."PID",
  p."Name" AS "Name",
  p."Gender" AS "Gender",
  COALESCE(cast_counts.cast_movie_count, 0) AS "cast_movie_count",
  COALESCE(dir_counts.director_movie_count, 0) AS "director_movie_count",
  COALESCE(prod_counts.producer_movie_count, 0) AS "producer_movie_count"
FROM "Person" p
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT "PID", COUNT(DISTINCT "MID") AS cast_movie_count
  FROM "M_Cast"
  GROUP BY "PID"
) cast_counts ON p."PID" = cast_counts."PID"
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT "PID", COUNT(DISTINCT "MID") AS director_movie_count
  FROM "M_Director"
  GROUP BY "PID"
) dir_counts ON p."PID" = dir_counts."PID"
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT "PID", COUNT(DISTINCT "MID") AS producer_movie_count
  FROM "M_Producer"
  GROUP BY "PID"
) prod_counts ON p."PID" = prod_counts."PID"
accepted.description: Aggregated counts of distinct movies per person for cast, director, and producer roles. One row per PID and role showing counts. Useful to compare activity across roles or to find prolific contributors. | Use for: Who are the most prolific actors/directors/producers; compare counts of movies by person and role; filter persons by minimum movie counts.

accepted.name: genre_movie_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  g."GID",
  g."Name" AS "Name",
  COUNT(DISTINCT mg."MID") AS "movie_count",
  AVG(m."rating") AS "average_rating",
  SUM(m."num_votes") AS "total_num_votes"
FROM "Genre" g
LEFT JOIN "M_Genre" mg ON g."GID" = mg."GID"
LEFT JOIN "Movie" m ON mg."MID" = m."MID"
GROUP BY g."GID", g."Name"
accepted.description: Aggregate counts and average ratings per genre. One row per GID exposing the genre Name, number of movies in that genre, average rating and total num_votes. Useful for ranking genres by popularity or quality. | Use for: Which genres have the most movies; which genres have highest average rating; genre popularity by votes.

accepted.name: movie_rating_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  "MID",
  "title",
  "year",
  "rating",
  "num_votes",
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY "rating" DESC) AS "rating_rank",
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY "num_votes" DESC) AS "votes_rank"
FROM "Movie"
accepted.description: Per-movie rank by rating with tie-aware RANK() and also rank by num_votes. One row per MID exposing two rank columns. Useful as a building block for Top-K queries by rating or votes. | Use for: Top-rated movies; most-voted movies; combined filtering by rating_rank or votes_rank.

accepted.name: movie_running_votes
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  "MID",
  "title",
  "year",
  "rating",
  "num_votes",
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY "year" ASC, "rating" DESC) AS "running_movie_index",
  COUNT(*) OVER () AS "total_movies"
FROM "Movie"
accepted.description: Running cumulative count of movies ordered by year then rating. One row per movie with a running_movie_index that can be used to select top-N chronologically/quality ordered subsets. Year is kept as provided (text). | Use for: Get first N movies by year then rating; compute percentiles by position; identify position of a movie in chronological/rating order.

accepted.name: movie_locations
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  m."MID",
  m."title",
  ml."LID",
  l."Name" AS "Name",
  ml."ID"
FROM "Movie" m
JOIN "M_Location" ml ON m."MID" = ml."MID"
LEFT JOIN "Location" l ON ml."LID" = l."LID"
accepted.description: Denormalized movie-to-location relation: one row per movie-location assignment with location Name. Useful for location-based filtering or counts of filming locations. | Use for: List locations for a movie; count movies shot in a location; filter movies by location name.

accepted.name: movie_people_roles
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT "MID", "PID", 'cast' AS "role", "ID"
FROM "M_Cast"
UNION ALL
SELECT "MID", "PID", 'director' AS "role", "ID"
FROM "M_Director"
UNION ALL
SELECT "MID", "PID", 'producer' AS "role", "ID"
FROM "M_Producer"
accepted.description: Wide relation enumerating people involved in each movie across cast, director, and producer roles. One row per MID/PID/role specifying the role type. Useful for role-based person queries and for unioning different role tables into a single people-in-movie view. | Use for: Find all people associated with a movie across roles; count distinct people per movie; filter people by role type.
